fields.failure: Card 118-2, diagnostic tools/bench/diag_c118_p1.py (a scratch donor VI built from EMPTY_v0.vi). It created a names constant on Get Controls.vi's 'Control Names' input with gscript.create_const_loop_term(value=<Python list of 20 strings Cam_pool00..Cam_pool19>): created_uid 101, err '', inv_err '' (diag_c118_p1.log:6-7). Gate A1b then read constant #101 back with diag_c118_p0.read_str and expected the bytes to end in the flattened Cam_pool00..19; it got hex 2600800000000001000400000001000000000000 and the run stopped at that fatal gate (diag_c118_p1.log:8-10).

case.known_answer: The READER failed, not (shown) the write: read_str reads Constant.Value through a base-class 'Constant' cast (OpConstValue_v1), which docs/NAMES.md:1157-1162 records as returning an EMPTY void variant, without error, for every non-String constant (numeric, boolean; the returned bytes are the void pattern - one type descriptor with code 0000 and no data, also seen on the VISA constants in diag_c105_const.json and ring #13245 in diag_c118_p0.json). So A1b could never pass on an array constant and says nothing about the write. Cheapest discriminating test: read #101 by a route that sees its type (a property node of its most specific class, ArrayConstant, or wire an indicator to it and run the donor), or read a known-filled array constant with the same reader - Cam_pool00..19 back = reader blind; empty array/wrong type = the COM list write failed. Settled: cycle 119 read the names constant back as Cam_pool00..19 through an array-capable reader.

case.known_answer: The summary has three defects. (1) T2's score also changed with effort (per-condition means low 0.5, medium 1, high 1, max 0.5; report_v1.md:8,27); report_v1.md:34 names only T5 and T6 as unchanged. (The second half - only T1's between-range exceeds repeat noise - is true, :34.) (2) The per-cycle cost comparison is confounded: a cycle's cost includes its material sessions, and cycles 89-91 ran Fable-low material (.claude/agents/material.md:8-10, $50-57 per cycle), two of them (89, 91) in the medium arm and one (90) in high (cycle_runner.log JUDGE-AB lines), so 'high is also cheaper' does not follow. (3) $17.59 is the total over 5 Fable cells and $15.24 over 10 Opus-high cells (report_v1.md:17,77); per cell Fable low ~$3.52 vs Opus high ~$1.52, about 2.3x - not 'about the same'.
